support_changes.analysis: Before us. Ūs is dative plural after ætforan.
Come before him. Him is dative singular, referring to the chief. Ætforan retains dative government here even with cuman; copy the whole supplied phrase.

Sir. Lēof is a substantival use of the strong masculine nominative singular adjective in direct address. This respectful address sense is supplied here; the previously taught meaning dear alone does not establish it.
A while ago; formerly. Use hwīlum ǣr as a complete earlier-time expression. Hwīlum here is part of this supplied expression, rather than the frequency meaning sometimes previously learned.

Fill their sacks with wheat. Gefyl is a singular command; hiera saccas is the accusative plural container, and mid hwǣte names the material with dative singular hwǣte. This full material-complement frame is supplied here.
In the morning. Morgen is accusative singular in this fixed temporal expression. Keep the whole phrase available; it does not introduce a general rule for every time expression with on.
